title: Careery’s new workspace
question: Choose the visual direction for the whole app. All options use the approved Base UI component stack and preserve existing behavior.

options.label: Production ledger
options.thesis: A precise workspace for turning career material into finished documents.
options.viewport: A narrow navigation rail, compact Resume rows, and a proof pane beside the active editor.
options.risk: The ruled structure needs generous reading measures to avoid feeling administrative.

raised.raise: Make every row and label earn its space without shrinking readable text.
Keep save and error states visible until resolved.
Give navigation and document language a consistent vocabulary.
Make the active document unmistakable without hiding row actions.
Keep section position visible throughout editing.

options.label: Proof desk
options.thesis: A focused writing tool with the finished document always close.
options.viewport: A compact workspace header above a section rail, editor, and persistent document preview.
options.risk: This is the most familiar document-editor structure and may feel less distinctive.

options.label: Dense reference workspace
options.thesis: Compact boxed sections expose many editing tasks at once.
options.viewport: A dense grid of career sections and recent Resumes.
options.risk: Density can overwhelm long bilingual writing.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity against a document-led workspace.

options.label: Application board
options.thesis: Resumes become rows with clear language, location, and edit status.
options.viewport: A ranked document list with persistent save-state markers.
options.risk: Departure-style ranking overemphasizes scheduling that Careery does not manage.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity because there is no travel or scheduling workflow.

options.label: Career route
options.thesis: A section legend guides progress through a Resume.
options.viewport: A numbered section rail beside a document proof.
options.risk: Map symbolism adds interpretation to straightforward editing.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity because editing is not navigation across terrain.

options.label: Document shelf
options.thesis: Resume tiles reveal document details on focus.
options.viewport: Rows of document previews grouped by Profile.
options.risk: Hidden metadata and horizontal rails slow scanning many similar Resumes.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity compared with explicit document rows.

options.label: Tabbed reference desk
options.thesis: Section tabs keep editing context visible.
options.viewport: A tab rail frames the active editor and proof.
options.risk: Physical layering and colorful boards compete with document content.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity when literal layering dominates.

options.label: Bilingual specimen desk
options.thesis: Typography and the live document lead the workspace.
options.viewport: A large document proof beside a narrow panel of wording and typography controls.
options.risk: The proof-first balance can crowd content organization.
options.case: Holds audience identification through professional document craft; the ledger offers clearer content organization.

canonCard.label: Familiar app workspace
canonCard.thesis: A conventional document dashboard executed with care.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar navigation, document list, and familiar split editor.
canonCard.risk: Deliberately similar to other productivity apps.
